issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata is provided anywhere in the record. `variables` is absent, and although `is_tabular: false` is appropriate for imaging and mass-spectrometry archives, the SEC-MS elution profiles and the perturb-seq cell atlas are tabular products whose columns are undocumented. A reuser cannot determine field names, units, or identifiers for cross-dataset linking.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add `variables` entries for at least the SEC-MS elution profile tables and the perturb-seq cell atlas, with variable identifiers, descriptions, and units.

issues_detected.description: The record labels six of ten file collections `collection_type: processed_data` and the description calls the release 'AI-ready data', but no preprocessing, cleaning, labeling, annotation, or imputation step is documented and no software is named that produced or transformed the distributed files. The only named pipeline (Cell Mapping Toolkit / MuSIC) is explicitly stated in `notes` to produce the computed cell maps that this release does NOT contain.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document the processing pipeline that converted the raw instrument output into the distributed processed_data archives, naming the software and versions used for AP-MS/SEC-MS search and quantitation and for perturb-seq count-matrix generation.

issues_detected.description: Only the container format is specified. `distribution_formats` declares ZIP / application/zip and `file_collections` records `compression: zip`, but the formats of the files inside the archives (e.g. TIFF/OME-TIFF for imaging, mzML/TSV for mass spectrometry, h5ad/MTX for perturb-seq) and character encoding are never stated. The record itself flags that even cm4ai_release_metadata.zip has no stated internal format.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add per-collection internal format and media_type (and encoding for text products) so that reuse does not require downloading multi-GB archives to discover their contents.

issues_detected.description: No release-level instance counts. `instances` enumerates four instance types but reports no counts of images, elution profiles, cells, or perturbations; `source_caveats` deliberately and correctly declines to reuse the project-level figures (53,788 images, 11,739 genes) as release totals, leaving the release's size characterized only by archive byte sizes and `total_file_count: 10`.
issues_detected.recommendation: State per-modality counts for this release (number of IF fields of view, number of SEC-MS fractions/proteins quantified, number of cells and targeted genes in the perturb-seq atlas).

issues_detected.description: `anomalies` and `missing_data_documentation` are absent. Known data-quality issues, outliers, failed runs, or missing-value patterns are not documented for any modality, even though `known_limitations` notes incomplete overlap of the protein sets interrogated across modalities.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add an `anomalies` block (e.g. excluded plates/wells, low-confidence identifications) and a `missing_data_documentation` block describing missing-value patterns in the MS and perturb-seq matrices.

issues_detected.description: `errata` is absent and `updates` carries only a schedule. What changed between the October 2025 release and this one is recoverable only from prose in `related_datasets.notes` ('did not include AP-MS data'), not from a change log or release notes slot.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add explicit change descriptions for Version 2.0 (AP-MS added; IF archives republished 2026-07-15) and an errata slot, rather than leaving version differences implicit in relationship notes.

issues_detected.description: The `conforms_to` value (RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE packaging) is carried from the preprint and the March/June 2025 releases; the record transparently states that the June 2026 release page does not itself restate the packaging format. The conformance claim is therefore inherited rather than verified for this version.
issues_detected.recommendation: Confirm and restate RO-Crate packaging for the June 2026 release, or scope the conformance claim to the metadata archive that carries it.

issues_detected.description: Temporal metadata is internally ordered (created_on 2025-02-27 < issued 2026-06-17 < last_updated_on 2026-07-15, matching the 2026-07-15 republication of the three IF archives), but the record notes the source page carries a Dataset Description dated 2025-06-30 and a Data Creation Date reused verbatim from earlier releases, so `created_on` is provenance of the collection rather than of this version's data.
issues_detected.recommendation: Distinguish collection-level deposit dates from this version's data-creation window.

issues_detected.description: No dedicated `download_url` is present, and the single entry in `distribution_formats.access_urls` (https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/) is a truncated API base with no file identifier, so it does not resolve to a downloadable object on its own. Access remains actionable only via the DOI, the publisher URL, and the stated Data Access API instruction for files over the 1.9 GB browser limit.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate `download_url` with the resolvable dataset landing/download URL and give per-file access URLs including Dataverse file identifiers.

issues_detected.description: `future_use_impacts` (rai:dataSocialImpact) is absent. Ethics documentation is unusually strong on process (named reviewers, Value-Sensitive Design methodology, Data Access Committee, CM4AI Life Cycle), but anticipated downstream social impacts of the released data and their mitigations are not analysed.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add `future_use_impacts` describing anticipated downstream impacts of AI models trained on these cell maps and planned mitigations.

issues_detected.description: `is_deidentified` states a status and its rationale ('non-clinical, from tissue cultures, cannot be matched with current knowledge to a human subject') rather than a named deidentification method. This is semantically appropriate for commercially sourced cell lines, but the KOLF2.1J donor provenance (healthy male Northern European donor, HipSci) is recorded only in `direct_collection`, and no re-identification risk assessment is linked to it.
issues_detected.recommendation: Cross-reference the cell-line donor provenance from `is_deidentified` and state whether any residual genotype-based re-identification risk was considered for the iPSC line.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C is well formed and its prefix (10.18130) is consistent with the stated publisher, the University of Virginia Dataverse/LibraData — identifier, publisher, and citation string agree.

Grant number 1OT2OD032742-01 parses correctly as an NIH award (OT2 activity code, OD institute, serial 032742, support-year suffix 01) and is semantically consistent with the stated Bridge2AI Functional Genomics Grand Challenge role.

The non-human-subjects determination is coherent across four independent slots: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=false, direct_collection.is_direct=false with a cell-line rationale, is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present=false, and sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present=false. These explicit negatives are reasoned rather than boilerplate.

License semantics are consistent end to end: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, data_use_permission=no_commercial_use, a prohibited_uses entry giving commercial restriction with the copyright-holder rationale, and ip_restrictions naming UC Regents and Stanford plus the Data Access Committee that supervises dual licensing.

Subset and file-collection identifiers cross-reference each other bidirectionally (each of nine subsets names its archive, each archive names its subset), and total_file_count=10 matches the ten file_collections entries including the metadata archive.

The representation-bias statement ('does not represent all biological variants seen in the population at large') is consistent with sampling_strategies.is_representative=false and its why_not_representative text — bias disclosure and sampling description agree.

Embargo status is consistently reported across known_limitations, raw_data_sources.access_details, and third_party_sharing, so a reuser learns which components are not yet retrievable before attempting access.

source_caveats demonstrates disciplined provenance hygiene: project-level cumulative counts are explicitly withheld from release-level slots, and the inherited conforms_to claim is flagged rather than silently asserted.

Governance and ethics contacts are resolvable and internally consistent: data_governance.committee_contact ORCID 0000-0003-4535-3486 matches creator Parker J, and ethical_reviews contacts match creators Ravitsky and Bélisle-Pipon with institutional email addresses.

Collection mechanisms are described at a level that supports replication (four IF channels with named stains, 6 guide RNAs per gene, inducible dCas9, 10x Genomics 3'HT readout), which is unusually specific for a multi-modal release.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: A single persistent identifier is used consistently as the dataset id, the doi slot, the latest-version pointer, and inside the citation string. Subsets and file collections are given stable fragment identifiers derived from the same DOI (e.g. doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#files-apms-paclitaxel), giving component-level addressability.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Matches 10.XXXX/... pattern. Prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) prefix and agrees with publisher https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/. No RRID is claimed, so no RRID pattern check applies.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description: ~1,300 characters naming each modality (perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS, immunofluorescence), each cell system (MDA-MB-468 ± paclitaxel/vorinostat; KOLF2.1J iPSC and NPC/neuron/cardiomyocyte derivatives), and the overarching objective.
sub_elements.quality_note: Well above the 200-character threshold and specific rather than generic: the description states exactly which modality covers which cell state, which is the information a reuser needs to decide relevance.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description content is semantically consistent with keywords, subsets, subpopulations.distribution, and file_collections; no modality is described that is not distributed, and every distributed archive corresponds to a described modality.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 27 terms including AI, AP-MS, breast cancer, Bridge2AI, cardiomyocyte, CRISPR/Cas9, iPSC, KOLF2.1J, MDA-MB-468, perturb-seq, SEC-MS, scRNAseq, subcellular imaging, paclitaxel, vorinostat
sub_elements.quality_note: Far exceeds the five-keyword threshold and spans domain, assay, cell line, perturbagen, and program dimensions. Includes both expanded and abbreviated forms (e.g. 'size exclusion chromatography' and 'SEC-MS'), which aids retrieval.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Every keyword is corroborated elsewhere in the record; no keyword stuffing with unsupported terms. Program context (Bridge2AI, CM4AI) is inferable from keywords and funders, as required.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://cm4ai.org/; publisher: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/; subsets: nine entries; file_collections: ten entries with MD5 checksums and sizes
sub_elements.quality_note: A resolvable project portal is given, and hierarchical structure is supplied through nine subsets each mapped to a named archive with checksum and byte size. The one weakness is that `page` points at the project portal rather than the version-specific Dataverse landing page for doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URL structure valid and domains plausible. Subset-to-file-collection references resolve within the document in both directions.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven typed entries — is_new_version_of doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, doi:10.18130/V3/DXWOS5; is_described_by doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311; is_referenced_by doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734; references doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3
sub_elements.quality_note: A full version lineage back to the first LibraData release is expressed with typed relationships, and each entry carries notes explaining what that predecessor contained. `parent_datasets` is not used, but the version chain and the nine internal subsets supply the hierarchy the sub-element asks for.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All target DOIs are well formed; 10.18130 (Dataverse), 10.1101 (bioRxiv), and 10.1038 (Nature) prefixes are consistent with the described targets. Relationship directions are used correctly — the U2OS Nature map is 'references' rather than 'is_new_version_of', a distinction the record explains.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 statement of share/adapt rights and attribution, non-commercial, and share-alike conditions; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; ip_restrictions.restrictions: 'Copyright for CM4AI data is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise noted; raw image data for spatial proteomics is copyright by The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University... commercial use requires a separate license negotiation with the copyright holder'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the license and the IP position are stated in operational detail, including which institution holds copyright over which data package and the existence of a Data Access Committee supervising dual licensing. This is actionable for a prospective commercial reuser.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: License terms, the machine-readable data_use_permission enum, and the prohibited_uses commercial entry are mutually consistent; no conflict between stated openness and stated restriction.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No; no export control or regulatory restriction is stated for the release.'; data_governance.committee_contact: Jillian Parker, ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu; data_governance.access_review_process: 'A Data Access Committee supervises ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use.'
sub_elements.quality_note: The regulatory determination is an explicit, sourced negative (FDA Regulated: No) rather than an omission, and it is paired with a named, contactable governance committee representative and a described access-review process — the governance-contact component this sub-element asks for. No confidentiality_level enum, hipaa_compliant, or other_compliance value is given, which is a real gap but a minor one for non-human-subject laboratory data.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The 'no restriction applies' record is consistent with human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=false and sensitive_elements_present=false. Governance contact ORCID matches the creator entry for Parker J, so the contact resolves.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/; distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/; distribution_formats.notes: 'All ten files in the release are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse. Files above the 1.9 GB browser download limit are obtained through the Data Access API.'; file_collections give exact filenames, MD5 checksums, and sizes
sub_elements.quality_note: Scored on the 'platform access instructions' branch of the sub-element: the repository, the resolvable DOI, the exact archive filenames with checksums, and the specific mechanism for retrieving the three multi-GB imaging archives are all stated, which is enough to retrieve the data. It is scored as a pass with reservation — the dedicated download_url slot is empty and the supplied API base is truncated.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Flagged as a correctness issue: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/ lacks a file identifier and does not resolve to an object by itself. The 1.9 GB browser limit note is consistent with the three IF archives (3.8 GB, 4.2 GB, 4.6 GB) exceeding it and the seven smaller archives not.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip; file_collections entries each carry compression: zip and collection_type (raw_data / processed_data / metadata)
sub_elements.quality_note: A format and a registered MIME type are specified, and each of the ten collections is typed as raw, processed, or metadata with checksum and size — enough to plan retrieval and verify integrity. Scored 1 for this access-oriented sub-element, while the absence of the archives' internal formats is charged against Element 3 sub-element 2, where interoperability is the question.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: media_type application/zip is the correct IANA type for the declared ZIP format; compression values agree with the .zip filenames throughout.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven typed entries with DOIs; external_resources: seven entries including https://cm4ai.org/, MassIVE, Figshare, NDEx, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, https://fairscape.github.io, http://integrativemodeling.org
sub_elements.quality_note: External deposits are linked at component granularity: SEC-MS and AP-MS to MassIVE, the CRISPRi atlas to Figshare, cell maps to NDEx, with the U2OS companion dataset's MassIVE (MSV000097168) and ProteomeXchange (PXD052362) accessions quoted. This is materially more useful than a bare list of links.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: External resource claims are consistent with raw_data_sources.access_details and third_party_sharing.notes, which name the same repositories for the same components.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on external evidence: distribution_formats is populated (ZIP/application/zip via UVA Dataverse), publisher is a public repository, and the license explicitly permits sharing and adaptation.
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Users are free to share... and adapt... under the conditions that appropriate credit is given... that the material is not used for commercial purposes; and that contributions built upon the material are distributed under the same license'; license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
sub_elements.quality_note: A named, standard, machine-identifiable license with the four conditions spelled out and an explicit statement that no additional legal or technological restrictions may be applied. Reuse for non-commercial research is unambiguously permitted.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: License restrictiveness is proportionate to the data type (non-human-subject laboratory data) and consistent with prohibited_uses and ip_restrictions; no contradiction between the NC clause and any claim of openness elsewhere.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats populated, accessible repository, reuse-permitting license).
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip. file_collections record only compression: zip. No file_collections.resources entries, no per-file format or media_type, no encoding anywhere in the record.
sub_elements.quality_note: Only the container is documented. ZIP is a standard archive format but carries no information about the data inside it, so a reuser cannot tell whether the imaging archives hold OME-TIFF or vendor formats, whether the MS archives hold mzML, MaxQuant tables, or TSV, or whether the perturb-seq atlas is h5ad, MTX, or CSV. The record itself concedes this for cm4ai_release_metadata.zip, whose internal format 'is not stated'. That is insufficient to support the interoperability purpose of this sub-element.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Inconsistent with the record's own 'AI-ready data' framing and with conforms_to: RO-Crate, which would normally imply a manifest of typed internal resources. No character encoding declared for any text product.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats populated, accessible repository, reuse-permitting license).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: 'RO-Crate. The CM4AI preprint and the March 2025 and June 2025 Dataverse releases state that CM4AI output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework...'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry ontology CURIEs B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/58/59/64 and B2AI_TOPIC:15/26/34
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels — packaging standard (RO-Crate), metadata schema (Bridge2AI data-sheets-schema with a w3id PURL), and controlled vocabulary use for substrate and topic on every instance. The record also discloses that the RO-Crate claim is inherited from the preprint and earlier releases rather than restated on the June 2026 page, which is honest scoping rather than overclaiming.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: RO_CRATE enum value agrees with the prose conforms_to; w3id URL is well formed; B2AI CURIE prefixes are used consistently across all four instance entries. The self-flagged inheritance of the claim is recorded as a content-accuracy warning rather than a failure.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats populated, accessible repository, reuse-permitting license).
sub_elements.evidence: No `variables` field appears anywhere in the record. The closest content is instances[].data_substrate / data_topic CURIEs and subsets[].description, neither of which defines variables or columns.
sub_elements.quality_note: No variable-level metadata, no data dictionary, and no identifiers for cross-dataset linking (no UniProt/Ensembl/HGNC identifier conventions stated for the proteins and genes that are the datasets' primary keys). This is the single largest interoperability gap in the record: integrating SEC-MS, AP-MS, IF, and perturb-seq components requires knowing the protein and gene identifier spaces used, and none is documented.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: is_tabular: false is a legitimate flag for imaging archives, but it does not excuse the SEC-MS elution profiles and perturb-seq cell atlas, which are inherently tabular products. Scored 0 on its own fields being absent, not by applicability exclusion.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: four categories — 'AI-ready data for functional genomics research', 'AI model training', 'Cellular process analysis', 'Analysis of cell architecture under perturbation' — each with examples; prohibited_uses: clinical decision-making/patient care without regulatory oversight, and commercial use, each with a prohibition_reason
sub_elements.quality_note: Both directions of guidance are given, and the prohibitions carry reasons rather than bare assertions: the clinical prohibition is grounded in the absence of regulatory oversight for laboratory data, and the commercial prohibition is grounded in the license and the copyright holders' reserved rights. `discouraged_uses` is absent, but the known_limitations entry noting that interpretation requires domain expertise partly fills that role.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Prohibited uses align with the license (NC) and with the FDA Regulated: No determination — the restrictiveness of the guidance matches the regulatory and ethical posture stated elsewhere.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition NOT met (E1 description and keywords name cell lines — MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J iPSC — not participants; E8 collection_mechanisms describe AP-MS, SEC-MS, confocal microscopy and CRISPRi screens, not recruitment). Governance condition MET on E2 evidence: data_governance.access_review_process states 'A Data Access Committee supervises ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use', data_governance.committee_contact names a contactable governance representative, license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission=no_commercial_use constrains reuse, and ip_restrictions require separate license negotiation for commercial use. Per the element preamble, a data access committee and an ethics contact are exactly the governance disjunct that opens sub-elements 1-2 for a dataset with no human participants.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries — 'Ethical Review for the release is carried out by Vardit Ravitsky (ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca)' with contact_person ORCIDs, and 'The Ethics Module employs a methodology inspired by Value-Sensitive Design (VSD)... including the construction of an axiological repository to guide the articulation of design standards and expectations'; human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false with rationale; data_governance.notes describing the CM4AI Life Cycle governance-milestone framework
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethical oversight is documented as an operating structure rather than an approval number, which is the appropriate form for non-human-subject cell-line work: named reviewers with institutional email addresses, a described review methodology, a Data Access Committee with a named contact, and a governance framework spanning data generation through AI development. A reader knows who to approach and on what basis distribution decisions are made.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistent with involves_human_subjects=false: no IRB approval number is claimed, and none is expected. Reviewer ORCIDs match the corresponding creator entries (Ravitsky 0000-0002-7080-8801; Bélisle-Pipon 0000-0002-8965-8153), so the contacts are verifiable. data_protection_impacts is absent, which is defensible here but leaves the DPIA component of the sub-element unaddressed.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same determination as sub-element 1: human-subjects condition not met on E1/E8 evidence, governance condition met on E2 evidence (Data Access Committee supervising distribution, named governance contact, non-commercial and IP constraints on reuse).
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'The release records De-identified Samples: Yes. CM4AI data are described as non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.'; direct_collection.collection_details: 'The MDA-MB-468 cell line is available from ATCC; the KOLF2.1J iPSC line was derived from a healthy male Northern European donor and is available from the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative (HipSci) resource.'
sub_elements.quality_note: No named technique (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) is given, but the record states the deidentification status, the basis for it, and the provenance of both cell lines, which together let a reader verify the claim rather than take it on trust. For commercially sourced, ethically obtained cell lines this is the substantively complete answer; a Safe Harbor citation would be a category error here.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Method appropriateness check passes: the deidentification rationale matches the data type (tissue-culture-derived molecular and imaging data with no linked clinical record). Consistent with human_subject_research.notes and sensitive_elements. Weakness flagged as a low-severity issue: no residual re-identification risk assessment is attached to the iPSC donor genotype, and the donor provenance sits in direct_collection rather than being cross-referenced here.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met on external evidence: E1 description and keywords reference commercially available cell lines (MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells, KOLF2.1J iPSCs and their NPC/neuron/cardiomyocyte derivatives) with no participants, patients, or clinical research; E8 collection_mechanisms describe instruments and assays (AP-MS, SEC-MS, ICC-IF confocal microscopy, CRISPRi lentiviral screens), not human participant recruitment; direct_collection.is_direct=false states data were not collected from individuals. Per #1060 the governance disjunct does not reach sub-elements 3-5: a Data Access Committee over a dataset with no participants does not create participants whose privacy could be protected.
sub_elements.evidence: No participant_privacy or reidentification_risk content, and no participants for it to concern. Excluded on E1/E8/direct_collection evidence, not on the emptiness of this sub-element's own fields.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Scoring 0 here would measure the dataset's subject matter (cell lines rather than people) rather than the quality of its documentation.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met on the same external evidence (E1 description/keywords name cell lines; E8 collection_mechanisms describe assays rather than recruitment; direct_collection.is_direct=false, 'Data were generated from commercially available, ethically sourced human cell lines rather than collected directly from individuals'). The governance disjunct does not extend to this participant-facing sub-element.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent is absent and there are no participants from whom consent could be obtained for this release; upstream donor consent for the KOLF2.1J line is a matter for the HipSci resource, which the record names.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. The record nonetheless characterizes the lines as 'ethically sourced' and names their source resources (ATCC, HipSci), which is the relevant upstream assurance for cell-line work.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met on the same external evidence (E1 cell-line description and keywords; E8 instrument-based collection mechanisms; direct_collection.is_direct=false). No enrolled population exists, so at_risk_populations and participant_compensation have no referent; the governance disjunct does not reach this participant-facing sub-element.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations and participant_compensation are absent, and no population was enrolled or compensated for this release.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator per the N/A convention; the excluded identities are Element 4 sub-elements 3, 4, and 5.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described

sub_elements.semantic_validation: Standard names are used correctly and in their proper roles (RO-Crate for packaging, EVI for provenance entailments, ARK for identifiers). The inherited-claim caveat on RO-Crate is carried as a content-accuracy warning.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats populated, accessible repository, reuse-permitting license).
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://cm4ai.org/; external_resources[0]: 'CM4AI project web portal at https://cm4ai.org/, providing project overview, data releases, tools, product documentation, publications, and learning materials'; pipeline user documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/; FAIRSCAPE 'described with a tutorial and installation instructions at https://fairscape.github.io'; maintainers list a program manager and a website-support contact with emails
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation links go beyond a landing page to include learning materials, a tutorial with installation instructions, and readthedocs user documentation for the analysis pipeline, plus named human contacts for project inquiries and website issues. This is the outreach infrastructure the sub-element asks for.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URLs are well formed with plausible domains; the portal claim is consistent with page. Documentation covers the tooling ecosystem even though, as noted under Element 8, that tooling is not tied to the files in this particular release.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats populated, accessible repository, reuse-permitting license).
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven entries each with an explicit relationship_type — four is_new_version_of (the October 2025, June 2025, March 2025, and original LibraData releases), is_described_by (the CM4AI preprint), is_referenced_by (the iPSC perturbation atlas preprint), and references (the Nature U2OS multimodal cell map, with its NDEx UUID, MassIVE MSV000097168, and ProteomeXchange PXD052362 accessions quoted)
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationships are typed with standard DataCite-style predicates and each carries a note explaining the substance of the connection, including what differed in each prior release. The Nature U2OS map is correctly typed as 'references' rather than a version relation, with the record explaining that it is a distinct dataset from overlapping investigators — a discrimination many datasheets get wrong.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship directions are semantically correct throughout; target DOIs are well formed and their prefixes match the described target types. The version chain is consistent with version_access.versions_available.

strengths: Exceptional provenance discipline: source_caveats records which tier of source each assertion came from, explicitly declines to reuse project-level counts as release-level totals, and flags that the RO-Crate conformance claim is inherited from earlier releases rather than restated on this one.

Complete and internally consistent identifier layer — DOI, id, citation, and latest_version_doi agree; nine subsets and ten file collections cross-reference each other bidirectionally; MD5 checksums and byte sizes are given for every archive.

Version lineage is fully addressable: every prior release is named with its own DOI and version label and typed with is_new_version_of, so a reuser can retrieve any historical version rather than only the current one.

Governance and ethics documentation is operational rather than nominal: a named Data Access Committee contact with email, named ethical reviewers with ORCIDs, a stated Value-Sensitive Design methodology, and a governance-milestone framework spanning data generation through AI development.

Collection and acquisition are described at replication-relevant granularity — IF channel-to-target assignments, 6 guides per gene with inducible dCas9, the 10x 3'HT readout chemistry, Human Protein Atlas antibodies, and automated fixation on a pipetting robot.
Licensing, IP, and use guidance form a coherent whole: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, no_commercial_use, per-institution copyright attribution, and prohibited uses each stated with their underlying reason.

Limitations disclosure leads with the most consequential fact — that the computed cell maps are not in this release — and states what the release is therefore suitable for, alongside per-component embargo status corroborated in three separate slots.
weaknesses: No variable-level metadata anywhere: no `variables`, no data dictionary, and no stated identifier space (UniProt, Ensembl, HGNC) for the proteins and genes that are the primary keys for integrating the four modalities.
Only container formats are documented — ZIP/application/zip — with no internal file formats or encodings, so a reuser cannot know what is inside multi-GB archives without downloading them.

No processing documentation at all: preprocessing, cleaning, labeling, annotation, and imputation slots are empty even though six of ten archives are typed processed_data and the release is described as AI-ready.

No software is named that produced or transformed the distributed files; the tooling that is documented is packaging (FAIRSCAPE), serving and visualization (NDEx, Cytoscape, ndex2), instrumentation (10x 3'HT kit), or a pipeline whose outputs the record states are not in this release (Cell Mapping Toolkit/MuSIC, IMP).
No release-level instance counts — no number of images, elution profiles, cells, perturbations, or baits — leaving the release's scale characterized only by ten archives and their byte sizes.
`anomalies` and `missing_data_documentation` are entirely absent, so no quality issue, exclusion, batch effect, or missing-value pattern is disclosed for any modality.
No errata or change log: what changed in Version 2.0 is recoverable only from a relationship note observing that the prior release lacked AP-MS data.
`download_url` is empty and the single access URL is a truncated Dataverse API base with no file identifier, so retrieval depends on resolving the DOI rather than on any link the record supplies.
`future_use_impacts` is absent, leaving anticipated downstream social impacts unanalysed despite otherwise strong ethics documentation.
recommendations: Add `variables` entries for the tabular products — SEC-MS elution profiles and the perturb-seq cell atlas — with variable identifiers, descriptions, units, and the protein/gene identifier namespaces used, so the four modalities can be joined.
Declare per-collection internal formats and media types (e.g. OME-TIFF, mzML, h5ad/MTX, TSV) and character encoding for text products, rather than documenting only the ZIP container.
Populate preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, and (where applicable) imputation_protocols for each modality, describing how raw instrument output became the archives typed processed_data.

Attach `used_software` with names and versions to those processing steps — the spectral search and quantitation software behind the AP-MS and SEC-MS tables, and the alignment and count-matrix software behind the perturb-seq atlas — distinguishing them from the packaging, serving, and instrumentation tooling already listed.
Report release-level counts per modality: fields of view and proteins imaged, fractions and proteins quantified, cells and genes targeted in the screens.

Add an `anomalies` block (excluded plates, wells, fractions, or cells; low-confidence identifications; batch effects) and a `missing_data_documentation` block describing missing-value patterns and how they should be handled.
Add explicit Version 2.0 change descriptions and an errata slot, noting the addition of AP-MS data and the 2026-07-15 republication of the three immunofluorescence archives.

Populate `download_url` with the version-specific Dataverse landing page and give per-file access URLs including Dataverse file identifiers; consider pointing `page` at the release landing page in addition to the project portal.

Add `future_use_impacts` analysing anticipated downstream social impacts of models trained on these cell maps, and record a re-identification risk consideration for the single-donor KOLF2.1J genotype.
Confirm and restate RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE packaging for this specific release, or scope the conformance claim to the metadata archive that carries it.
Add variable-level metadata with identifiers and the protein/gene namespaces used for cross-modality joins.
Declare internal file formats and encodings per collection instead of only the ZIP container.
Document the preprocessing and cleaning pipeline that produced the archives typed processed_data.
Name the software and versions that produced or transformed the released files, distinct from packaging, hosting, and instrumentation tooling.
Report release-level instance counts per modality.
Document anomalies, exclusions, and missing-data patterns.
Provide Version 2.0 change descriptions and an errata slot.
Populate download_url with resolvable per-file or version-specific access links.
Add future_use_impacts and a re-identification risk note for the single-donor iPSC line.
Restate RO-Crate conformance for this release or scope the inherited claim.
